_meta.purpose: SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria control catalogue in CatalogFile shape, so applyCatalogFile creates the framework, its requirements, the templates, their requirement links and the pack together.
_meta.why: Production served SOC2- — 7 templates whose titles restate the criterion ('Specifies objectives'), each carrying the five generic placeholder tasks. These 29 TSC- templates are real controls and were never delivered anywhere. This file replaces that offering.
_meta.grounding: Requirement titles and summaries come from src/data/libraries/soc2-2017.yaml so the two cannot drift. Task content is grounded in each template's own description — the library is thin for SOC 2 (a one-line COSO paraphrase, no checklist or artifacts).
_meta.packStrategy: Reuses SOC2_BASELINE rather than creating SOC2_CORE. The retirement of the seven SOC2- criterion-restatement templates is a separate operator step, not a seeder action — seeders upsert, they do not delete, and deleting customer-visible catalogue rows should be a reviewed action with before/after counts rather than a side effect of a deploy.

templates.title: Code of conduct and annual acknowledgement
templates.description: Maintain a written code of conduct covering ethical behaviour, confidentiality, and acceptable use, require every employee and contractor to acknowledge it at hire and annually thereafter, and act on reported violations. Implements SOC 2 CC1.1.

title.en: Compile the list of employees and contractors who must acknowledge the code

description.en: Pull the population from the HR system and from wherever contractor records are held — they are usually separate systems, and contractors are the group most often missed, which is what makes a 100% acknowledgement rate meaningless. Record each person's name, start date, employment type and the code version they last acknowledged. This list is the denominator every later task is measured against. Attach the list dated at the point it was compiled.

evidenceHint.en: Dated acknowledgement population list covering employees and contractors, giving start date, employment type and last version acknowledged per person

text.en: Export the active employee roster from the HR system with start dates.
Add contractors and temporary staff from the systems holding their records.
Mark each person with the code version they most recently acknowledged.
Date the list and hold it as the population for this period's run.

title.en: Write the code of conduct sections covering ethical behaviour, confidentiality and acceptable use

description.en: The control names three subjects the code must cover, so treat them as a checklist against the current draft rather than assuming the existing document reaches all three: ethical behaviour, confidentiality of company and customer information, and acceptable use of company systems. Where a subject is covered only by implication, write it out plainly enough that a violation of it is decidable by somebody who was not in the room. Attach the draft with the section covering each of the three subjects identifiable.

evidenceHint.en: Draft code of conduct with the ethical behaviour, confidentiality and acceptable use sections marked

text.en: Check the current draft against each of the three required subjects.
Write out any subject the code covers only by implication.
State prohibited conduct clearly enough for a breach to be decidable.
Route the draft through legal review before it goes for approval.

title.en: Collect a dated acknowledgement from every person at hire and at the annual re-issue

description.en: Issue the current version of the code to everyone on the population list and retain one acknowledgement record per person carrying their name, the version acknowledged and the date. New joiners acknowledge as part of joining rather than waiting for the next annual run. Chase the outstanding names until the register and the population list agree, and record a reason against anyone who never acknowledged. Attach the acknowledgement register export for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Acknowledgement register export: one row per person with the code version acknowledged and the date

text.en: Issue the current code version to everyone on the population list.
Record the name, version and acknowledgement date for each response.
Issue the code to new joiners as part of the joining process.
Chase outstanding names until the register matches the population list.
Record a reason against anyone who did not acknowledge.

title.en: Record the investigation and outcome of each reported conduct violation

description.en: For every conduct violation reported during the period, keep a case record naming the date it was reported, how it was investigated, the conclusion reached and the action taken. Hold the detail that identifies individuals separately from the summary record, so the control can be evidenced to an auditor without exposing personal data the auditor has no need to see. General Counsel advises on the investigation; the case record stays with People Ops. Attach the summary case log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Conduct case log for the period: report date, investigation summary, conclusion and action taken, with identifying detail held separately

title.en: Record management's annual review and approval of the code, naming the approver and date

description.en: Acknowledgements are collected against one specific version of the code, so that version needs a recorded approval standing behind it — the evidence here is the decision, not the document. Put the current version to the approving manager together with the changes made since the last approval and the conduct cases seen in the period, then record who approved it, on what date, and which version they approved. A version issued with no recorded approval leaves a year of acknowledgements attached to an unapproved document. Attach the approval record.

evidenceHint.en: Approval record naming the approver, the approval date and the code version approved

text.en: Summarise the changes made since the previous approval.
Include the period's conduct cases in the review pack.
Put the current version to the approving manager for decision.
Record the approver, the approval date and the version approved.

templates.title: Board and management oversight of security
templates.description: Hold a recurring governance meeting at which management reports the security and compliance posture — open risks, incidents, control failures, audit findings — to a body independent of day-to-day operations, and minute the decisions taken. Implements SOC 2 CC1.2.

title.en: Name the oversight body's members and record their independence from day-to-day operations

description.en: The control requires reporting to a body independent of day-to-day operations, so start by writing down who that body is: its members, the role each holds, and the basis on which each is independent of the operations being reported on. Where a member also runs part of what is being overseen, record how that is handled — a body composed of the people being overseen evidences nothing. Attach the membership record, with the terms of reference alongside it where one exists.

evidenceHint.en: Oversight body membership record showing each member's role and the basis of their independence from the operations being reported on

title.en: Define the standing agenda management must report against at every oversight meeting

description.en: Fix the contents of the report so each meeting covers the same ground and a gap becomes visible: movement in the risk register, incidents raised and closed, control tests that failed, audit findings, and the status of remediation still open. Name who produces each section, and carry a standing item for the actions left open at the previous meeting. Attach the agreed standing agenda or the terms-of-reference extract that carries it.

evidenceHint.en: Standing agenda for the oversight meeting naming each required reporting section and the person who produces it

text.en: List the reporting sections the control names as required.
Name the owner who produces each section of the pack.
Add a standing item for the actions left open last time.
Have the oversight body agree the agenda and minute that it did.

title.en: Assemble the posture pack of open risks, incidents, control failures and audit findings

description.en: For each meeting, build the pack the standing agenda calls for: what moved in the risk register since the last meeting, the incidents raised and how they closed, which control tests failed, the open audit findings, and where remediation stands. Report the failures as plainly as the successes — a pack showing only green gives an oversight body nothing to challenge, and the challenge is what the control is asking to see. Attach the pack as circulated, carrying its date and the period it covers.

evidenceHint.en: The dated governance reporting pack as circulated, covering risk register movement, incidents, failed control tests, audit findings and open remediation

text.en: Extract risk register movement since the previous meeting.
List the incidents raised in the period and how each closed.
List the control tests that failed and the remediation owner for each.
Add the open audit findings with their current status.
Circulate the dated pack to members ahead of the meeting.

title.en: Minute each oversight meeting with the decisions taken, their owners and due dates

description.en: Write the minute so a reader who was not present can see what the body was told, what it challenged and what it decided. Every decision gets a named owner and a due date; a minute recording only that the pack was noted evidences attendance rather than oversight. Carry forward any item left open at the previous meeting and record where it now stands. Attach the approved minutes for the meeting.

evidenceHint.en: Approved minutes recording attendance, the challenges raised, the decisions taken, and the owner and due date of each action

title.en: Track the open oversight actions to closure and re-table anything still outstanding

description.en: Keep the actions from the minutes as a live list rather than a paper trail: each action, its owner, its due date, its current status, and the evidence that closed it. Before the next meeting, check every open action and put the ones that have slipped back in front of the body with the reason they slipped. Attach the action log showing what closed during the period and what remains open.

evidenceHint.en: Oversight action log showing each action's owner, due date, status and the evidence that closed it

templates.title: Personnel screening and onboarding
templates.description: Screen candidates before they are granted access — identity, right to work, references, and, where the role and local law permit, a criminal-record or credit check — and complete security onboarding before production access is granted. Implements SOC 2 CC1.1.

title.en: Record which screening checks apply to each role, with the legal basis and retention period

description.en: Write the matrix that decides what happens for any given hire: for each role band, which of identity, right to work, references, criminal-record and credit checks apply, the legal basis for running each in the jurisdictions you hire in, and how long the outcome is kept. The control makes the criminal-record and credit checks conditional on the role and on local law, so the matrix has to record where they may not be run at all rather than leaving that to a recruiter's judgement. Attach the screening matrix.

evidenceHint.en: Screening matrix: role band, checks required, legal basis per hiring jurisdiction, and retention period for each outcome

text.en: List the role bands you hire into and the access each receives.
Set which checks apply to each band, including where none apply.
Record the legal basis for each check in each hiring jurisdiction.
Record how long each screening outcome is retained, and where.
Record the version of the matrix issued and the date recruiters worked to it.

title.en: Add a screening-complete gate to the access request that grants production access

description.en: What this control requires is an ordering — screening and security onboarding come before production access, not alongside it. Put that ordering into the request workflow, so a production grant cannot be approved until People Ops has confirmed screening completed and onboarding is done, instead of relying on the approver remembering. Record what the approver must see before they can approve. Attach the configured workflow or the approval form showing the gate.

evidenceHint.en: The access request workflow or approval form showing the screening and onboarding confirmation required before a production grant

title.en: File the screening outcome for every new hire with the date each check completed

description.en: For each person who joined in the period, retain the outcome of every check the matrix required for their role, with the date it completed and who ran it. Keep the outcome — passed, or passed with a noted exception and who accepted it — rather than the underlying report where that report holds more personal data than the control needs. Attach the screening record set covering the period's joiners.

evidenceHint.en: Screening records for the period's joiners: person, checks run, completion date and outcome for each check

title.en: Confirm each joiner completed security onboarding and signed the confidentiality agreement

description.en: Security onboarding and the confidentiality agreement are both evidenced per person rather than by pointing at the onboarding programme. Record the completion date of the onboarding session and hold the signed agreement against the person's record. Chase anyone who reached their start date without both, and record the date they closed it. Attach the joiner completion record for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Joiner record per new hire showing the security onboarding completion date and the signed confidentiality agreement

title.en: Compare each production access grant against the screening completion date for that hire

description.en: This is the test that proves the ordering actually held. Take the production access grants made during the period, match each to the person it was made for, and check that the screening and onboarding dates precede the grant date. Every case where they do not is an exception: record it with the reason, the access granted early, and what was done about it. Attach the comparison with the exceptions listed.

evidenceHint.en: Comparison listing each new hire, their screening and onboarding completion dates, their first production access grant date and any exception

text.en: Export the production access grants made during the period.
Match each grant to the person it was made for.
Compare the grant date against the screening and onboarding dates.
List every grant that preceded completion, with reason and outcome.

templates.title: Security roles, responsibilities, and accountability
templates.description: Document who is accountable for each security and compliance responsibility — policy ownership, control operation, incident command, vendor review — keep the assignments current as people move, and hold owners to their commitments. Implements SOC 2 CC1.1 and CC1.2.

title.en: List every security and compliance responsibility that needs a named owner

description.en: Build the list before assigning anything, because the omissions are what this control exists to catch. The control names four kinds to start from — policy ownership, control operation, incident command and vendor review — and each expands: one row per policy, one per control in the control matrix, one per incident-command role, one per vendor review. A responsibility that never reaches this list is never assigned and never missed. Attach the responsibility list.

evidenceHint.en: Responsibility list covering policy ownership, control operation, incident command and vendor review, one row per responsibility

title.en: Assign a named owner and a named backup to each responsibility in the matrix

description.en: Fill the matrix so every row carries a person, not a team and not a job title nobody currently holds. Name a backup as well, so an owner's absence does not stop the control operating. Where one person ends up holding an implausible number of rows, report that to management rather than recording an assignment that will not be honoured. Attach the completed responsibility assignment matrix, dated and version-marked.

evidenceHint.en: Responsibility assignment matrix showing a named owner and a named backup for every responsibility

title.en: Collect each owner's written acceptance of the responsibility and the evidence it produces

description.en: Send each owner the rows assigned to them and ask them to confirm in writing that they accept them and understand what evidence they must produce. Acceptance is what turns an assignment somebody else made into a commitment, and it surfaces the rows an owner did not know they held. Record the confirmation date per owner and follow up those who do not reply. Attach the acceptance records collected in the period.

evidenceHint.en: Written acceptance per owner naming the responsibilities accepted and the date each was confirmed

title.en: Move every responsibility held by a leaver or a mover to a new named owner

description.en: Treat a role change or a departure as a trigger on this matrix, not only on the access review. When People Ops notifies one, find every row that person holds, name the replacement owner and obtain their acceptance — doing it before access is removed means the outgoing owner is still there to hand over. Record the change and its date. Attach the matrix change log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Matrix change log listing each leaver or mover, the responsibilities reassigned, the new owner and the date of the change

title.en: Reconcile the responsibility matrix against the control matrix and the current staff roster

description.en: Two failure modes hide in a matrix nobody checks: a control or policy with no row at all, and a row owned by somebody who has left or moved. Run both comparisons — every entry in the control matrix has an owner here, and every owner named here is still employed and still in the role. List the gaps found with the action taken to close each. Attach the reconciliation.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation listing responsibilities with no owner, owners who have left or changed role, and the action taken on each

text.en: Check every control in the control matrix has an owning row here.
Check every policy in the policy set carries a named owner.
Check each named owner against the current staff roster.
Record each gap found and the reassignment that closed it.

templates.title: Information security policy set
templates.description: Maintain an approved set of information security policies covering acceptable use, access control, data classification, change management, incident response, and vendor management; review and re-approve them at least annually and publish them where all staff can reach them. Implements SOC 2 CC2.1.

title.en: List the policies in the set and map each required subject to the policy that covers it

description.en: The control names six subjects the set must cover: acceptable use, access control, data classification, change management, incident response and vendor management. Build a register with one row per subject naming the policy that covers it, that policy's current version and its owner — and leave the row visibly empty where nothing covers the subject, because the empty row is the finding this task exists to produce. Attach the policy register.

evidenceHint.en: Policy register mapping each of the six required subjects to the covering policy, its current version and its owner

text.en: Create one row for each of the six required subjects.
Name the policy covering each subject and its current version.
Name the owner accountable for keeping each policy current.
Leave the row empty where no policy covers the subject, and raise it.

title.en: Record the version, approver and approval date on the front of every policy

description.en: Give every policy in the set the same front matter, so a reader can tell which version they are holding and who approved it: version number, approval date, approver, and the date it next falls due for review. Without it an auditor cannot distinguish an approved policy from a draft, and staff cannot tell whether the copy saved to their laptop is still current. Attach the policy set showing the front matter on each document.

evidenceHint.en: The policy set with version number, approver, approval date and next review date carried on each document

title.en: Publish the approved versions where all staff can reach them and notify staff of material changes

description.en: Publication is part of this control rather than an afterthought — a policy nobody can find has not been communicated. Put the approved versions in the location every employee and contractor can reach, remove or clearly mark superseded copies, and send a notification describing what materially changed and what people now do differently. Attach the publication record together with the notification as sent.

evidenceHint.en: Publication record showing each policy version live on the staff-accessible location, with the change notification as sent

text.en: Upload each approved version to the staff-accessible policy location.
Remove or mark superseded versions so only the current one is used.
Describe what materially changed in terms staff can act on.
Send the notification and retain it with its date and recipients.

title.en: Compare each policy against how the organisation actually operates and log where it has drifted

description.en: Walk each policy with the team that lives under it and note every place the document and the practice disagree — a policy naming a tool that was replaced, an approval step nobody performs, a retention period the platform does not enforce. Each disagreement gets resolved one way or the other: change the practice, or change the policy. Record which was chosen and who owns the change. Attach the drift log.

evidenceHint.en: Drift log per policy: the clause, the practice that differs from it, the resolution chosen and its owner

title.en: Obtain the annual re-approval of every policy in the set and record the version approved

description.en: The control requires review and re-approval at least annually, so the year ends with a decision recorded per policy: the approver, the date, and the version they approved. Put the drift log in front of the approver alongside the document, so the approval is made on what changed rather than on a title page. Any policy reaching the end of the year with no recorded approval is an exception to report. Attach the approval record for the set.

evidenceHint.en: Approval record listing each policy, the version approved, the approver and the approval date

templates.title: Security awareness training
templates.description: Deliver security awareness training to every employee and contractor at onboarding and at least annually, cover the threats the organisation actually faces (phishing, social engineering, data handling), and track completion against a named list. Implements SOC 2 CC2.1 and CC1.1.

title.en: Build the roster of every employee and contractor the training must reach

description.en: The control asks for completion tracked against a named list, so the list has to exist before anything is assigned. Take active employees from the HR system and contractors from wherever their records live, and record each person's start date and whether they are due the onboarding round or the annual round. Someone who joined mid-period needs the onboarding assignment, and counting them in the annual round is how they disappear. Attach the roster dated at the point it was compiled.

evidenceHint.en: Dated training roster listing every employee and contractor with their start date and the round due to them

title.en: Update the curriculum to cover phishing, social engineering and data handling

description.en: The control names three subjects the training must cover and ties them to the threats the organisation actually faces, so refresh the content against what happened here: the phishing lures that reached staff, the incidents raised in the last period, and the data-handling mistakes behind them. Replace the generic examples with those, and add any new regulatory obligation that has landed since the last revision. Attach the curriculum or module list showing the three subjects covered and the date it was last revised.

evidenceHint.en: Curriculum or module list covering phishing, social engineering and data handling, showing its revision date

text.en: Review the incidents and phishing reports from the last period.
Rewrite the examples around lures and mistakes seen here.
Check each of the three named subjects is covered by a module.
Add any new regulatory obligation the training must now cover.
Record the revision date and what changed since the last version.

title.en: Assign the training at onboarding and at the annual round, then chase non-completers to closure

description.en: Assign against the roster rather than a distribution list, so a person who joined last week is assigned as part of joining and everyone else is assigned in the annual round. Chase the outstanding names, escalating to their manager where they stay outstanding, until every person on the roster is either complete or carries a recorded reason. Attach the completion report for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Training completion report: one row per person on the roster with the assignment date and either a completion date or a recorded reason

title.en: Run a simulated phishing exercise and coach the people who fail it

description.en: Run the simulation against the roster, record who clicked, who submitted credentials and who reported it, and give those who failed follow-up coaching rather than only a statistic. Keep the result at a level that supports coaching without becoming a disciplinary record — that is what stops people reporting the next one. Attach the simulation result together with the record of coaching delivered.

evidenceHint.en: Phishing simulation result showing click, submission and report rates, with the record of follow-up coaching delivered

title.en: Reconcile the completion report against the roster and list who is still outstanding

description.en: A completion percentage is computed against whoever was assigned, so a person missing from the assignment never shows as incomplete — this reconciliation is what catches them. Match the completion report to the roster line by line, list everyone on the roster with no assignment and everyone assigned but not complete, and record what was done about each. Attach the reconciliation.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation of the training roster against the completion report, naming everyone unassigned or incomplete and the action taken

templates.title: Internal and external reporting channels
templates.description: Provide and publicise channels through which staff, customers, and external researchers can report security concerns — including an anonymous internal channel and a monitored external security contact — and ensure reports reach an accountable owner within a defined time. Implements SOC 2 CC2.1.

title.en: List every reporting channel with its audience, accountable owner and defined time

description.en: One row per channel this control requires — the anonymous internal route for staff and the monitored external security contact for customers and researchers — naming who the channel is for, the mailbox, form or hotline a report physically lands in, the accountable owner who has to pick it up, and the defined time within which a report has to reach that owner. That defined time is what the rest of this control is measured against, so it belongs written down here rather than left to whoever happens to be watching the inbox. Attach the channel register dated at the point it was compiled.

evidenceHint.en: Reporting-channel register: channel, audience, routing destination, accountable owner and the defined time within which a report must reach them

text.en: Record the anonymous internal route and where a staff report physically lands.
Record the external security contact customers and researchers are told to use.
Name the accountable owner who must pick up a report on each channel.
State the defined time within which a report must reach each owner.
Date the register so the arrangement in force at any point is identifiable.

title.en: Publish the anonymous internal reporting route where staff will find it

description.en: Put the internal route in the places staff already read — the handbook, the intranet security page and the induction pack are the usual ones — and state plainly what the channel is for, that it can be used without giving a name, and who receives what is sent. A channel that exists but is known only to the team that built it does not meet the publicity this control asks for. Attach the published page or handbook section together with the date it went live, and note any location where the route is deliberately not advertised.

evidenceHint.en: Published internal page or handbook section showing the anonymous route and who receives it, with its publication date

title.en: Publish the monitored external security contact for customers and researchers

description.en: Make the external contact reachable by someone with no existing relationship: a security address or form on the public site, reachable from the pages a customer or an external researcher would try first. Say what the contact is for and that reports are triaged, and point it at the destination recorded in the channel register rather than at a personal mailbox. Attach the published page with its URL and confirm the address resolves to the monitored destination rather than to an alias nobody reads.

evidenceHint.en: Public security-contact page with its URL and publication date, plus confirmation the address routes to the monitored destination

title.en: Log every report received against its channel, owner and acknowledgement date

description.en: Keep one log across both channels: what came in, which channel it arrived on, who it was routed to, the date it was acknowledged and how it was resolved. Record the acknowledgement date even when the report turns out to be noise, because the log is the only thing that shows reports reached an accountable owner inside the committed time. Keep entries free of identifying detail where the reporter used the anonymous route, so the log does not undo the anonymity the channel promises. Attach the log covering the period.

evidenceHint.en: Reporting log for the period: report reference, channel, routed owner, acknowledgement date and outcome

title.en: Send a test report through each channel and record where it landed

description.en: Submit a marked test report through the internal route and through the external contact, then follow it: confirm it arrived at the destination named in the register, that the accountable owner saw it, and how long acknowledgement took against the committed time. Submit as an outsider would — from a personal device for the external contact, without using an internal shortcut — so the test exercises the same path a real reporter uses. Attach the test record with timestamps and, where the committed time was missed, what was changed.

evidenceHint.en: Channel test record per channel: submission timestamp, arrival destination, acknowledging owner and elapsed time against the commitment

text.en: Submit a marked test report through the anonymous internal route.
Submit a marked test report through the external security contact.
Confirm each landed at the destination named in the channel register.
Measure elapsed time to acknowledgement against the committed time.
Record any misroute or missed commitment and the fix applied.

title.en: Review the period's reports against the defined time and fix what missed it

description.en: Read the log back against the register: for every report in the period, whether it reached its accountable owner inside the defined time, and where it did not, what delayed it — an unmonitored destination, an owner who had left, a routing rule nobody updated. Record the change made in response to each miss, because a channel that misses the defined time and carries on unaltered is the case this control exists to surface. Attach the review listing the reports that missed the defined time, the cause of each and the fix applied.

evidenceHint.en: Review of the period's reports against the defined time: reports that missed it, the cause of each and the change made in response

templates.title: Annual enterprise risk assessment
templates.description: Perform a documented risk assessment at least annually that states the entity's objectives, identifies threats to them across the in-scope systems, rates likelihood and impact on a defined scale, and records the treatment decision and owner for each risk. Implements SOC 2 CC3.1.

title.en: Record the objectives the risk assessment is measured against

description.en: Before a single risk is listed, write down what the assessment is protecting: the entity's objectives in force for the period being assessed — the commitments made to customers and the system requirements that follow from them, where they take that form — in the words they are actually stated in. A threat is only assessable against something, and a risk to an unstated objective cannot be rated. Cite where each objective is stated so the set can be checked rather than taken on trust. Attach the objectives statement dated at the start of the assessment.

evidenceHint.en: Dated objectives statement listing each objective in force for the period and the document it is stated in

title.en: List the systems in scope of the risk assessment with their owners

description.en: Enumerate the systems the assessment covers — the production services, the supporting infrastructure and the third-party components the commitments depend on — with the team or person accountable for each. This list is the population the threat identification works through, so a system missing here is a system no risk will ever be raised against. Record anything deliberately excluded and the reason, in the same list rather than in a separate note. Attach the scope list.

evidenceHint.en: In-scope systems list giving an owner per system, with the exclusions and the stated reason for each

title.en: Define the likelihood and impact scale and how the two produce a risk score

description.en: Write the scale down before rating anything: what each likelihood level means in observable terms, what each impact level means against the objectives recorded in scope, and the rule that combines the two into a score. Without it, two assessors rate the same threat differently and this year's register cannot be compared with last year's. Attach the scale definition with the date it was adopted, so the version used in any given assessment is identifiable.

evidenceHint.en: Risk scale definition giving each likelihood and impact level, its meaning, and the rule that combines them into a score

text.en: Write what each likelihood level means in observable terms.
Write what each impact level means against the recorded objectives.
State the rule that combines likelihood and impact into a score.
Date the scale so the version used in each assessment is identifiable.

title.en: Rate every identified threat against the scale and record the score

description.en: Work through the in-scope systems, identify the threats and vulnerabilities that could stop the recorded objectives being met, and rate each on the defined likelihood and impact scale. Record the reasoning that produced the score and not only the number, so a later reader can tell whether the rating still holds. Cover every system on the scope list, and state where a system produced no risk rather than letting it be silently absent. Attach the completed assessment worksheet.

evidenceHint.en: Completed risk assessment worksheet: threat, affected system, likelihood, impact, score and the reasoning recorded per risk

title.en: Record the treatment decision and named owner for each rated risk

description.en: For every risk carrying a score, record the decision taken — accept, mitigate, transfer or avoid — the person accountable for carrying it out, and where mitigation is chosen, what the mitigation is. An accepted risk needs the same rigour as a mitigated one: name who accepted it, not just that it was accepted. Attach the risk register extract showing a decision and a named owner on every row.

evidenceHint.en: Risk register extract with treatment decision, named owner and, where mitigation was chosen, the mitigation recorded on every rated risk

title.en: Confirm every register entry carries a rating, a treatment and an owner before closing the assessment

description.en: Read the register back against the scope list and the scale: every in-scope system represented or explicitly cleared, every risk scored on the defined scale, every risk carrying a treatment decision and a named owner. Record what was missing and what was done about it, because the gaps found in this pass are the ones an auditor would otherwise find first. Attach the completeness check with its findings and the date the assessment was declared complete.

evidenceHint.en: Completeness check listing rows missing a rating, a treatment or an owner, their resolution, and the assessment completion date

templates.title: Fraud risk consideration
templates.description: Explicitly consider fraud scenarios — misappropriation, unauthorised data disclosure for gain, management override of controls — as part of the risk assessment, and record the controls relied on to address each. Implements SOC 2 CC3.1.

title.en: List the fraud scenarios considered, including misappropriation and management override

description.en: Write down the plausible fraud scenarios for this business rather than fraud in the abstract: misappropriation of assets, unauthorised disclosure of customer data for gain, and management override of controls, plus any scenario the business model makes specific — who could do it, what they would take, and which system they would do it through. A scenario nobody names cannot be mapped to a control, so this list is the population the next task works through. Attach the scenario list with the date it was compiled.

evidenceHint.en: Dated fraud scenario list naming, per scenario, the actor, the asset or data at stake and the system involved

text.en: Name the misappropriation scenarios this business model allows.
Name the scenarios where data could be disclosed for personal gain.
Name the scenarios where management could override a control.
Record the actor, the asset at stake and the system for each scenario.

title.en: Map each fraud scenario to the control relied on and flag the ones with none

description.en: Against every scenario on the list, name the existing control that would stop or surface it and say which of the two it does — prevention and detection are not interchangeable when the actor is trusted. Where no control answers a scenario, mark it as a gap rather than stretching an unrelated control to cover it; the gaps are the output this control is looking for. Attach the mapping showing scenario, control, whether the control prevents or detects, and the unmapped scenarios.

evidenceHint.en: Fraud scenario to control mapping marking each control preventive or detective, with the unmapped scenarios listed as gaps

title.en: Minute the fraud discussion held as part of the risk assessment

description.en: This control requires fraud to be considered explicitly, which means there has to be a record that the consideration happened: who took part, which scenarios were discussed, what was concluded about each, and what was carried forward. Hold it inside the risk assessment rather than as a separate exercise, so the fraud conclusions land in the same register as everything else. Attach the minutes with the attendee list and the date.

evidenceHint.en: Dated minutes of the fraud consideration with attendees, the scenarios discussed and the conclusion recorded against each

title.en: Raise a risk-register entry for every fraud scenario with no control mapped

description.en: Take each gap from the mapping and put it in the risk register where it is tracked alongside everything else — the scenario, its rating, the treatment decided and the owner. A gap recorded only in the fraud mapping is a gap nobody is chasing between assessments. Attach the register entries created, each referenced back to the scenario it came from.

evidenceHint.en: Risk register entries raised for the unmapped fraud scenarios, each citing its source scenario and naming an owner

title.en: Assess where a privileged user could override a control undetected

description.en: Walk the paths where someone holding administrative or approval authority could bypass a control — disabling a check, approving their own change, editing a record directly — and for each one say what would notice. Where the answer is nothing, record it as an exposure together with the monitoring that would close it. This is the scenario least likely to be caught by a control set built around an untrusted outsider. Attach the override analysis naming each path and the detective control covering it.

evidenceHint.en: Management-override analysis: each bypass path, the detective control that would surface it, and the paths nothing currently covers

text.en: Identify the roles holding administrative or approval authority.
Trace how each could disable, bypass or self-approve a control.
Name the detective control that would surface each bypass.
Record the bypass paths nothing would currently notice.

templates.title: Risk assessment of significant change
templates.description: Assess the security and availability impact of significant changes — new products, material architecture changes, new sub-service organisations, acquisitions, regulatory change — before they take effect, and feed the result into the risk register and the change record. Implements SOC 2 CC3.1 and CC8.1.

title.en: Write the trigger criteria that make a change significant enough to assess

description.en: Turn the categories this control names — new products, material architecture changes, new sub-service organisations, acquisitions and regulatory change — into criteria a team can apply without a judgement call: what counts as material, what counts as a new sub-service organisation, and who decides a borderline case. Teams judging case by case is how a significant change reaches production unassessed. Attach the issued criteria with the date they took effect and the place change requesters read them.

evidenceHint.en: Issued significance criteria covering each named change category, the decision route for borderline cases, and the effective date

text.en: Write the test for a new product or material architecture change.
Write the test for engaging a new sub-service organisation.
Write the test for an acquisition or a change in regulation.
Name who decides when a change sits on the borderline.
Date the criteria and publish them where change requesters work.

title.en: Add the significance question to the change record so a qualifying change cannot skip it

description.en: Put the trigger criteria in the path of the change itself: a required field on the change record asking whether the change meets any of them, and a link to the assessment where the answer is yes. This control requires the assessment before the change takes effect, which only holds if the change process asks the question rather than relying on somebody remembering to. Attach the change template or workflow configuration showing the field, its required state and the link.

evidenceHint.en: Change record template or workflow configuration showing the significance field, its required state and the link to the assessment

title.en: Assess each qualifying change for security and availability impact before it takes effect

description.en: For every change meeting the criteria, write the assessment before the change is live: what the change introduces or alters, the security and availability risks that follow, and the mitigations planned. Cite the change record it belongs to, so the assessment is read beside the authorisation the change was actually made under rather than sitting apart from it. Where the change brings in a sub-service organisation, cover what it will hold and what it will reach. Attach the completed assessments for the period, each dated ahead of the change taking effect.

evidenceHint.en: Completed change risk assessments for the period, each naming the risks and mitigations, citing its change record, and dated before the change went live

title.en: Record the risks arising from each assessed change in the risk register

description.en: Carry the assessment's output into the register rather than leaving it in the change ticket: add or update the risk entries the change creates, rate them on the standing scale, and cite the change record so the two can be read together. A residual risk accepted at change time and recorded nowhere else disappears the moment the change closes. Attach the register entries with their change references.

evidenceHint.en: Risk register entries created or updated from the period's change assessments, each citing its change record reference

title.en: Compare the period's changes against the trigger criteria to find unassessed ones

description.en: Take the changes actually made in the period from the change record, apply the criteria to each, and check that everything qualifying carries an assessment dated before it took effect. Record the changes that qualified and were not assessed, and what was done about them — this reconciliation is the only thing showing the trigger works rather than merely exists. Attach the reconciliation with its findings.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation of the period's changes against the criteria, listing qualifying changes with no prior assessment and their resolution

templates.title: Continuous control monitoring
templates.description: Monitor whether controls are operating — automated checks where possible, scheduled control tests otherwise — on a defined cadence, and record the result of each evaluation together with the evidence examined. Implements SOC 2 CC4.1.

title.en: Assign every control a monitoring method and a test frequency

description.en: Build the monitoring schedule the rest of this control runs from: one row per control, the method used to monitor it — an automated check where the evidence can be collected by machine, a scheduled manual test otherwise — the frequency, and who performs it. Record why each frequency was chosen, so a control monitored less often than its neighbours reads as a decision somebody took rather than an oversight. Attach the schedule covering every control in the catalogue.

evidenceHint.en: Control monitoring schedule: control, monitoring method, frequency, assigned tester and the reason for the frequency chosen

title.en: Configure the automated checks for the controls the schedule marks automatable

description.en: Build or enable the check for each control the schedule says can be monitored by machine, so the evaluation runs on its own cadence and writes a result nobody has to remember to produce. Point each check at the evidence a tester would otherwise gather by hand, and make it record what it examined rather than only pass or fail. Where a control is marked automatable but no check can express it, send the row back to the schedule as a manual test instead of leaving it monitored by nothing. Attach the exported check configuration.

evidenceHint.en: Exported automated check configuration per control, plus the list of controls returned to manual testing because no check could express them

text.en: Take the controls the schedule marks as automatable.
Configure each check to record the evidence it examined.
Set each check to run on the frequency the schedule states.
Return any control no check can express to manual testing.
Export the running configuration and file it with its date.

title.en: Write the test procedure for each manually tested control

description.en: For every control the schedule leaves to a manual test, write what the tester actually does: the population to sample, the evidence to examine, and what a pass looks like against the control's own requirement. A test whose method lives in the tester's head produces a different answer each time the tester changes. Keep each procedure short enough to be followed inside the time its frequency allows. Attach the procedures, one per manually tested control.

evidenceHint.en: Manual test procedures naming, per control, the population to sample, the evidence to examine and the pass condition

title.en: Run the scheduled control tests and record the result and evidence examined

description.en: Work the schedule for the period: run each check or test that falls due, record pass or fail with the date and the tester, and attach the evidence actually examined beside the result — this control asks for the evidence, not only the verdict. Where a test could not be run, record that as its result rather than leaving the row blank, because a blank row and a passing row look the same at a glance. Attach the monitoring log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Monitoring log for the period: control, test date, tester, result and the evidence examined attached to each row

title.en: Compare the tests performed against the monitoring schedule and record the gaps

description.en: At period end, put the monitoring log next to the schedule and find the rows that never ran: controls whose automated check was disabled, whose tester left, or whose frequency was quietly missed. Record each gap, the reason for it and when it will be covered. A schedule nobody reconciles reports the coverage it was written with rather than the coverage it achieved. Attach the coverage reconciliation.

evidenceHint.en: Coverage reconciliation listing scheduled tests not performed in the period, the reason for each and the date it will be covered

templates.title: Control deficiency tracking and remediation
templates.description: Track every identified control deficiency — from control testing, audits, penetration tests, or incidents — in one register with a severity, an owner, and a remediation due date, and report ageing items to management until they are closed. Implements SOC 2 CC4.1.

title.en: List the sources that feed deficiencies into the register and who submits from each

description.en: Name every activity that can produce a deficiency — control testing, internal and external audits, penetration tests and incidents — and for each one the person responsible for putting its findings into the register and the point at which they do it. This control asks for one register regardless of which activity found the item, and a source with no named submitter is how a penetration test report ends up tracked only inside the report. Attach the source list.

evidenceHint.en: Deficiency source list naming each feeding activity, its named submitter and the point at which findings are entered

title.en: Set up the deficiency register with severity, owner and due date on every row

description.en: Create the single register this control requires, with the fields it names as mandatory on every entry — source, description, severity, owner and remediation due date — and define the severity levels so two people rate the same finding the same way. Where a field can be left blank, the register fills with rows nobody can act on and nobody can chase. Attach the register together with its field definitions and the severity scale.

evidenceHint.en: Deficiency register with its field definitions and severity scale, showing source, severity, owner and due date as mandatory fields

text.en: Make source, severity, owner and due date mandatory fields.
Define each severity level so two people rate a finding alike.
Add the status values that distinguish open from closed.
Point every source on the source list at this one register.

title.en: Record every deficiency found in the period with its source, severity and owner

description.en: Enter the findings each source produced during the period, whichever activity found them, with the severity rated on the defined scale, the owner who will remediate, and the due date agreed with that owner. Enter them as they arrive rather than in a sweep before reporting, so the register can be read as the current state at any moment rather than only on reporting day. Attach the register export for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Deficiency register export for the period showing source, severity, owner and remediation due date on every entry

title.en: Attach the evidence of the fix before moving a deficiency to closed

description.en: Do not close a deficiency on the owner's word that it is fixed: record what was actually done and attach the evidence that the fix is in place — the changed configuration, the corrected record, or a re-run of the control's own test where that is what settles it — against the register row before the status moves to closed. Where the evidence shows the deficiency is still live, leave the row open and record the second attempt against it, so a reopened item stays visible rather than being closed twice. Attach the closure evidence for every deficiency closed in the period.

evidenceHint.en: Closure evidence attached to each deficiency closed in the period: what was done, the date, and who confirmed the fix was in place

title.en: Report ageing and overdue deficiencies to management in the governance pack

description.en: Write the section that shows management what is not getting fixed: open deficiencies by severity, how long each has been open, which are past their remediation due date and who holds them. Keep the same items visible period after period until they close — an ageing report showing only this period's arrivals hides exactly the items this control exists to surface. Attach the pack section as presented, with its date.

evidenceHint.en: Governance pack section showing open deficiencies by severity, age, overdue status and owner, dated as presented

title.en: Reconcile the register against each source's findings to show none was dropped

description.en: Take each source on the list — the period's control tests, audit reports, penetration test findings and incident records — and check that every finding it raised appears in the register. Record the ones that did not, whether they were entered late or judged out of scope, and who decided. This is the check that the single register is actually single. Attach the reconciliation.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation per source listing findings raised, findings present in the register, and the resolution of every difference

templates.title: Independent security assessment
templates.description: Obtain an independent assessment of the in-scope environment at least annually — a penetration test or an equivalent third-party technical review — scoped to the production system, and remediate findings against severity-based SLAs. Implements SOC 2 CC4.1.

title.en: Define the assessment scope as the production in-scope environment

description.en: Write down what the assessor is being pointed at: the production systems, applications, external network ranges and interfaces that carry the in-scope service, plus anything deliberately excluded and why. Scope drift is what makes a clean report meaningless, so the exclusions matter as much as the inclusions. Attach the dated scope statement that the engagement will be run against.

evidenceHint.en: Dated scope statement naming the production systems, applications and network ranges in scope, with exclusions and their justification

title.en: Agree the rules of engagement and independence terms with the assessor

description.en: Settle with the third-party assessor, in writing before testing starts, the methodology, the test window, the source addresses testing will come from, the escalation contact for a live-issue finding, and the assessor's confirmation that they are independent of the teams that built and run the environment. Attach the engagement letter or statement of work recording what was agreed.

text.en: Record the testing methodology the assessor will follow.
Fix the test window and the source addresses testing originates from.
Name the escalation contact for a finding that needs immediate action.
Obtain the assessor's written confirmation of independence from the build and run teams.
Record the agreed terms in the engagement letter before testing begins.

title.en: Record the remediation SLA that applies to each finding severity

description.en: State, per severity band the assessor uses, how long remediation may take, and record which severity scale those bands come from so a finding maps to a window without argument. This is the yardstick every later triage and the closing check are measured against, so it has to exist before the report arrives rather than being negotiated finding by finding. Attach the severity-to-SLA table as it stands for this engagement.

evidenceHint.en: Severity-to-SLA table giving the remediation window for each severity band and the severity scale those bands are keyed to

title.en: Triage every reported finding to a severity, an owner and a remediation date

description.en: Take the assessor's report line by line: accept or challenge the severity with a written reason, name the individual who owns the fix, and set the due date from the SLA table rather than from convenience. Raise each one in the deficiency register so it is tracked with everything else rather than in the report PDF. Attach the assessor's report together with the register extract showing all findings from this engagement.

evidenceHint.en: The assessor's dated report for the engagement, with the deficiency register extract listing every finding, its agreed severity, named owner and SLA-derived due date

text.en: Copy each finding from the report into the deficiency register.
Accept or challenge the assessor's severity, recording the reason either way.
Name an individual owner for each finding, not a team alias.
Set the due date from the severity-to-SLA table.
Record any finding whose due date already falls outside its SLA window.

title.en: Obtain the assessor's retest confirmation for the high-severity findings

description.en: Once the high-severity fixes are deployed, have the original assessor — or an internal reviewer independent of whoever built the fix — retest and state in writing whether each one is closed, partially closed or still open. A developer's assertion that a fix works is not a retest. Attach the retest report or the assessor's written confirmation.

evidenceHint.en: Retest report or written assessor confirmation stating the post-fix status of each high-severity finding

title.en: Check every finding reached its recorded disposition within its SLA

description.en: At engagement close, walk the deficiency register against the assessor's report and confirm nothing was quietly dropped: every finding is closed, formally risk-accepted with a named acceptor, or still open with a date. Compare each closure date against the SLA table and list the breaches. Attach the close-out summary with the SLA comparison.

evidenceHint.en: Engagement close-out summary reconciling the report to the register, with closure dates compared against the SLA and breaches listed

templates.title: Control matrix and control ownership
templates.description: Maintain a matrix listing every control relied on for the SOC 2 report, the criterion it addresses, its owner, its operating frequency, and the evidence it produces, and keep it current as controls are added or retired. Implements SOC 2 CC5.1.

title.en: List every control relied on for the SOC 2 report as a matrix row

description.en: Build the matrix from the controls that actually operate, one row each, with the control reference and a one-line statement of what it does. A control that exists but is not being relied on for the report stays out, and one that is relied on but has never been written down is exactly what this task is for. Attach the matrix export as it stands at compilation.

evidenceHint.en: Dated control matrix export with one row per control relied on for the report

title.en: Map each control row to at least one Trust Services criterion

description.en: Put the criterion reference on every row, using the criterion the control genuinely addresses rather than the nearest plausible one. Rows that map to nothing are either out of scope or mis-stated, and both need resolving here rather than at audit. Attach the mapped matrix and a short note on any row you could not place.

text.en: Add the criterion reference column to every matrix row.
Match each control to the criterion it genuinely addresses.
List the rows that map to no criterion and decide whether they are in scope.
Record a one-line rationale for any mapping that is not self-evident.

title.en: Complete the owner, operating frequency and evidence columns for every row

description.en: For each control name the individual accountable for it operating — a person, not a team alias — the frequency it runs at, and the artefact that proves it ran, including where that artefact is stored. A row with an owner but no named evidence is the row that produces nothing when the auditor asks. Attach the completed matrix.

evidenceHint.en: Control matrix with owner, operating frequency, evidence artefact and storage location populated on every row

title.en: Update the matrix when a control is added or retired, recording the reason

description.en: Keep the matrix current as the estate changes: when a control goes live add its row, and when one is superseded record why it went and confirm in the same edit that its criterion is still covered by something else. Date each change so the matrix has a history rather than only a present state. Attach the change history for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Dated matrix change history for the period, showing each addition and retirement with its reason and the criterion coverage after the change

title.en: Check both directions of coverage between controls and criteria

description.en: Run the matrix two ways: every in-scope criterion must have at least one control, and every control must carry a criterion. The first direction finds gaps in the report; the second finds rows nobody can justify keeping. Record both lists and what was done about each entry. Attach the coverage check with its exceptions.

evidenceHint.en: Two-way coverage check listing criteria with no control and controls with no criterion, each with its resolution

templates.title: Segregation of duties
templates.description: Separate conflicting duties so no single person can both make and approve a sensitive change — code deployment, privileged access grants, payments, and audit-log administration — and compensate with detective monitoring where separation is impractical. Implements SOC 2 CC5.1 and CC6.1.

title.en: List the duty pairs that must never be held by one person

description.en: Write down each conflicting pair and the systems it applies to, covering at minimum code deployment, privileged access granting, payments and audit-log administration. State the pair as two concrete acts — who can perform, who must approve — rather than as a principle, because a principle cannot be tested against a permission list. Attach the duty-pair definition.

evidenceHint.en: Duty-pair definition listing each conflicting act pair and the systems on which it applies

text.en: Name the two acts in each pair: who performs and who approves.
Cover code deployment, privileged access grants, payments and audit-log administration.
List the systems on which each pair is enforceable.
Note any pair that cannot be separated with today's tooling.

title.en: Configure each named system to require a second person for the conflicting act

description.en: Turn the pairs into enforced settings: branch protection that refuses a self-approved merge, access grants that need an approver other than the requester, payment release that needs a second authoriser, and audit-log administration held away from whoever is monitored by it, with the finance owner confirming the payment-system setting. Capture the configuration from each system as proof it is enforced rather than expected. Attach the settings capture.

evidenceHint.en: Configuration capture from each system showing the second-person requirement enforced on the conflicting act

text.en: Set deployment approval so the author cannot approve their own change.
Require an approver other than the requester on privileged access grants.
Enable second-authoriser release on the payment system.
Restrict audit-log administration away from the monitored population.
Capture each setting as dated evidence of enforcement.

title.en: Record the detective control covering each pair that cannot be separated

description.en: Where the team is too small or the tooling will not enforce it, name the compensating detective control for that pair — the alert, the report or the after-the-fact review that would surface an abuse — together with who reviews its output. An unseparated pair with no named detective control is an accepted risk and should be recorded as one. Attach the compensating-control record.

evidenceHint.en: Compensating-control record naming the detective control and reviewer for every unseparated duty pair

title.en: Run the detective monitoring for the unseparated pairs and record what it returned

description.en: Execute each compensating detective control for the period, read its output, and record the result even when it is empty — a monitoring control with no evidence of having run is indistinguishable from one that was never enabled. Investigate anything it surfaced and record the outcome. Attach the monitoring output with the reviewer's notes.

evidenceHint.en: Dated detective-monitoring output for the period with the reviewer's notes and the outcome of anything it surfaced

title.en: Test the current permission assignments against the documented duty pairs

description.en: Pull the live role and permission assignments from each system in the pair list and look for anyone holding both sides. Report violations by person and system, and record whether each was removed, reassigned or accepted with its compensating control. Attach the conflict test with its remediation column.

evidenceHint.en: Conflict test results per system, naming every person holding both sides of a pair and the remediation for each

templates.title: Access provisioning and timely revocation
templates.description: Grant access only on documented approval from the resource owner, based on job role and least privilege, and revoke all access on termination or role change within the committed time — driven from an authoritative HR record, not from ad-hoc notification. Implements SOC 2 CC6.1.

title.en: List the in-scope systems with the resource owner who approves access to each

description.en: Name, per system, the individual whose approval is required before access is granted. Where a system has no obvious owner, that is the finding — an access request with nobody entitled to approve it gets approved by whoever is quickest. Attach the system-to-owner list used to route requests.

evidenceHint.en: System-to-owner list naming the approving resource owner for every in-scope system

title.en: Define the least-privilege access profile granted for each job role

description.en: For each role that gets access, state which systems it receives and at what privilege level, so a joiner's grant is a decision made once rather than copied from whoever sat nearest. Record what is deliberately excluded from the baseline and must be requested separately. Attach the role-to-access profile.

evidenceHint.en: Role-to-access profile stating the systems and privilege level granted to each job role, with the extras that need separate request

text.en: List the job roles that receive access to in-scope systems.
State the systems and privilege level in each role's baseline.
Mark the access that is excluded and must be requested separately.
Have the resource owners confirm their system's entry in the profile.

title.en: Configure the revocation trigger to fire from the authoritative HR record

description.en: Wire revocation to the termination and role-change records HR maintains, so access is cut or reduced on the recorded date rather than on someone remembering to send a message. Confirm the feed carries both event types with their effective dates and reaches every in-scope system, and note any system still revoked by hand. Attach the trigger configuration and the list of manual exceptions.

evidenceHint.en: Revocation trigger configuration showing the HR termination and role-change records as its source, with the list of systems still revoked manually

title.en: Record the resource owner's approval before each access grant is made

description.en: Keep the approval with the request: who asked, which role and privilege level was granted, which owner approved, and the date — captured before the account is created rather than reconstructed afterwards. Attach the approval records for the grants made in the period.

evidenceHint.en: Access request records for the period, each showing the requester, the role granted, the approving owner and the approval date

title.en: Log the revocation time against the HR date for each leaver and role change

description.en: For every leaver and role change in the period, record the effective date from the HR record and the timestamp at which access was actually removed or reduced in each in-scope system, and flag any gap that exceeds the revocation window the policy commits to. Attach the revocation log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Revocation log for the period, giving the HR termination or role-change date and the per-system revocation timestamp, with breaches of the committed window flagged

title.en: Compare the accounts in each in-scope system against the active personnel list

description.en: Take the account listing from each system and the active personnel roster, and work the difference: accounts belonging to nobody currently employed, and staff holding access the role profile does not grant. Investigate each and record the disposition rather than only the count. Attach the reconciliation with its findings.

evidenceHint.en: Account-to-personnel reconciliation per system, listing every unmatched account and what was done about it

templates.title: Authentication and multi-factor enforcement
templates.description: Require unique named accounts, enforce a password policy that rejects weak and known-breached credentials, and require multi-factor authentication for remote access, administrative access, and access to the production environment. Implements SOC 2 CC6.1.

title.en: List the systems that fall under remote, administrative or production access

description.en: Enumerate the systems in each of the three categories the control names, because MFA coverage can only be claimed against a population that has been written down. Mark which category or categories each system falls into, and note anything reachable from outside the corporate network. Attach the categorised system list.

evidenceHint.en: Categorised system list marking each in-scope system as remote, administrative or production access

title.en: Configure the password policy to reject weak and known-breached credentials

description.en: Set the policy in each identity provider so it refuses credentials that appear in a known-breach corpus and those that fail the documented strength rules, and confirm the check runs at the point a password is set rather than only at first login. Attach the configured policy from each provider.

evidenceHint.en: Password policy configuration from each identity provider showing the strength rules and the breached-credential check

text.en: Enable the breached-credential check in each identity provider.
Set the strength rules to match the documented standard.
Confirm the check fires when a password is set or changed.
Capture the resulting configuration from every provider.

title.en: Enforce multi-factor authentication across the three access categories

description.en: Turn MFA on for every system in the categorised list, and check enforcement is unconditional rather than a prompt a user can dismiss or an option the account holder chooses. Where a system genuinely cannot enforce it, record the exception with its approver and the compensating control instead of leaving it unremarked. Attach the enforcement state per system.

evidenceHint.en: Per-system MFA enforcement state, with any exception recorded alongside its approver and compensating control

title.en: Capture the enforced authentication settings from each identity provider

description.en: Take a dated export or screenshot of the live MFA and password settings from every identity provider in the period and compare it against the documented standard, so drift is caught by the capture rather than at audit. Record any difference and the ticket raised to correct it. Attach the dated configuration capture.

evidenceHint.en: Dated configuration capture per identity provider for the period, with any drift from the documented standard noted

title.en: Identify every account not tied to a named person and record its custody

description.en: Work through the account listings for shared and service accounts, justify each one that stays, and record who holds its credential, where that credential is stored, and how it is rotated. An account with no named custodian is the one that survives every leaver process. Attach the shared and service account register.

evidenceHint.en: Shared and service account register giving the justification, named custodian, credential store and rotation arrangement for each account

templates.title: Periodic user access review
templates.description: Have resource owners review who holds access to each in-scope system at least quarterly, confirming that both the account and its privilege level are still warranted, and remove or downgrade access that is not. Implements SOC 2 CC6.1 and CC4.1.

title.en: Name the system owner who must review access for each in-scope system

description.en: Assign each in-scope system to the individual who will make the keep, downgrade or remove decision for its accounts. Reviews sent to a team inbox come back unowned, so the entry must be a person. Attach the reviewer assignment list covering every in-scope system.

evidenceHint.en: Reviewer assignment list naming the accountable system owner for every in-scope system

title.en: Export the dated user and privilege listing that forms the review population

description.en: Pull the current account listing from each in-scope system, including the privilege or group each account holds, and date it at the moment of export — the date is what ties the reviewer's decisions to a defensible population. Attach the export per system as the review population.

evidenceHint.en: Dated user and privilege listing exported per in-scope system, used as the review population

title.en: Record each owner's decision for every account and its privilege level

description.en: Have the system owner rule on both questions the control asks — should this person still have an account, and is this privilege level still warranted — and capture a decision against every line, not just the ones being changed. A returned listing with blanks is an incomplete review. Attach the completed review sheet with the owner's attestation.

evidenceHint.en: Completed review sheet per system carrying a keep, downgrade or remove decision on every account, with the owner's attestation and date

text.en: Send each owner their system's dated listing.
Require a decision on every line, including accounts left unchanged.
Ask separately about the privilege level, not only the account.
Have the owner attest and date the completed sheet.
Chase any listing returned with blank lines before closing the round.

title.en: Remove or downgrade the access an owner did not confirm

description.en: Action every remove and downgrade decision from the returned sheets, raising a change record for each so the removal is traceable to the review that ordered it, and re-check the account afterwards to confirm the change took effect. Attach the change records with the post-change listing.

evidenceHint.en: Change records for every removal and downgrade ordered by the review, with the post-change listing confirming they took effect

title.en: Confirm every in-scope system completed its review for the quarter

description.en: Compare the reviews returned against the list of in-scope systems and their assigned owners, and name any system that did not complete one — an unreviewed system is a gap in the quarter, not an administrative loose end. Record the reason and the recovery date for each. Attach the completion summary.

evidenceHint.en: Quarterly review completion summary listing every in-scope system, whether its review completed, and the recovery date for any that did not

templates.title: Encryption in transit and at rest
templates.description: Encrypt customer data in transit over untrusted networks using current TLS configurations, and at rest in databases, object storage, and backups, with keys held in a managed key store under restricted access and a documented rotation schedule. Implements SOC 2 CC6.1.

title.en: Inventory every endpoint, database, bucket and backup copy holding customer data

description.en: The control covers data in transit over untrusted networks and at rest in databases, object storage and backups, so the population has to include all four surfaces rather than the production database alone. Record for each entry what customer data it holds, whether it is reached over an untrusted network, and which encryption mechanism is claimed for it today. Anything left off this list is a surface the later verification tasks will never look at. Attach the inventory, dated at the point it was compiled.

evidenceHint.en: Dated encryption scope inventory listing every public endpoint, database, object store and backup copy holding customer data, with the encryption mechanism claimed for each

text.en: List the public endpoints that carry customer data over untrusted networks.
List the databases and object stores holding customer data at rest.
List every backup copy and the storage it is written to, including offsite copies.
Record the encryption mechanism claimed for each entry on the list.
Date the inventory and hold it as the population the later tasks sample from.

title.en: Record the TLS protocol versions and cipher suites approved for public endpoints

description.en: State which TLS versions and cipher suites an in-scope endpoint may negotiate and which are refused, so that a current TLS configuration is a written standard someone can be measured against rather than a judgement made afresh at each review.
