Cover every endpoint in the inventory, including those terminating TLS at a load balancer or CDN rather than at the application. Attach the configuration standard as issued, carrying its version and issue date.

evidenceHint.en: Issued TLS configuration standard naming the permitted protocol versions and cipher suites and the versions refused, carrying its version and issue date

title.en: Record every key in the managed key store with its rotation schedule and permitted users

description.en: One row per key: what it protects, the managed key store holding it, which principals may use it, which may export it, and the rotation interval documented for it. The control requires keys held under restricted access on a documented rotation schedule, and neither is evidenceable while the schedule lives in a runbook and the access list only in an IAM policy nobody has read out. Attach the key register showing the current holders of use and export rights for each key.

evidenceHint.en: Key register, one row per key, giving its purpose, the key store holding it, the principals with use and export rights, and the documented rotation interval

title.en: Scan the public endpoints and record the TLS version and cipher each negotiates

description.en: Run the scan against every endpoint in the inventory and capture what it actually negotiates, then repeat it forcing each protocol version the standard refuses, to confirm the connection is rejected rather than downgraded. A configuration file asserting a minimum TLS version is not evidence that a legacy listener elsewhere is refusing anything. Attach the scan output for the period showing the endpoint, the negotiated version and cipher, and the result of each refused-version attempt.

evidenceHint.en: Endpoint TLS scan output for the period showing, per endpoint, the negotiated protocol version and cipher and the outcome of each attempt at a refused version

text.en: Scan every endpoint listed on the encryption scope inventory.
Record the protocol version and cipher each endpoint negotiates.
Retry each endpoint forcing a protocol version the standard refuses.
Record which endpoints downgraded instead of refusing the connection.
Raise a ticket for every endpoint whose result differs from the standard.

title.en: Capture the at-rest encryption state of each database, object store and backup copy

description.en: For every at-rest entry in the inventory, pull the encryption state from the platform itself — the console or API output showing encryption enabled and the key it uses — rather than from a design document, and include the backup copies, which are the entry most often encrypted by a different mechanism than the source they were taken from. Record any store found unencrypted together with the remediation ticket raised against it. Attach the collected evidence for the period.

evidenceHint.en: At-rest encryption evidence pack for the period showing, per database, bucket and backup copy, the platform-reported encryption state and the key it uses

title.en: Reconcile key use and rotation records against the register's schedule and access list

description.en: Take the key store's own logs for the period and check them against the register: every key rotated on or before its documented interval, every principal that used or exported a key present on the permitted list, and every permitted principal still needing the right. Record each discrepancy with its disposition — rotation performed late, access removed, or an exception recorded with its reason. Attach the reconciliation covering every key in the register.

evidenceHint.en: Key rotation and access reconciliation giving, per key, the last rotation date against its documented schedule and any principal that used or exported it without being on the permitted list, each discrepancy carrying its disposition

templates.title: Physical access and secure media disposal
templates.description: Restrict physical access to facilities and equipment holding in-scope data to authorised personnel, review the authorised list periodically, and destroy or securely wipe media before disposal or reuse — including equipment handled by a sub-service organisation. Implements SOC 2 CC6.1.

title.en: List the facilities and equipment holding in-scope data, including any run by a sub-service organisation

description.en: Record every location and piece of equipment where in-scope data is held or processed — offices with on-premises equipment, storage rooms, and the data centres a hosting or colocation provider operates on the entity's behalf. Mark against each whether physical access is controlled by the entity itself or by a sub-service organisation, because the two are evidenced differently: one by the badge and key register, the other by the provider's attestation. Attach the dated list.

evidenceHint.en: Dated list of facilities and equipment holding in-scope data, marking for each whether physical access is controlled by the entity or by a named sub-service organisation

title.en: Record the authorised holder of every badge, key and door credential for in-scope areas

description.en: Build the authorised-access register the periodic review is run against: one row per credential, naming the holder, the areas it opens, the date access was granted and the business reason for it. Include contractors, cleaners and anyone holding a physical key rather than a badge, since those are exactly the holders a badge-system export will not show and therefore the ones a review driven by that export can never remove. Attach the register.

evidenceHint.en: Physical access register listing every badge, key and door credential with its holder, the areas it opens, the date access was granted and the reason for it

title.en: Write down the sanitisation method required for each type of media before disposal or reuse

description.en: The control requires media to be destroyed or securely wiped before it leaves the entity or is handed to another user, so record which of the two applies to each media type in use — laptop drives, server disks, removable media, and equipment returned to a leasing or hosting provider — and what record each method produces. Name who performs each method, whether in-house or a disposal vendor. Attach the issued procedure with its version and issue date.

evidenceHint.en: Issued media sanitisation procedure naming, per media type, whether destruction or secure wipe applies, who performs it and the record the method produces

title.en: Record a destruction certificate or wipe log for every device retired in the period

description.en: For each device or piece of media that left service, capture the asset identifier, the date, the method applied and the certificate or wipe log produced, so a retired asset can be traced from the asset register through to its disposal record. Where a sub-service organisation performed the destruction, hold their certificate rather than a note that they were asked. A retirement with no matching record is the gap this task exists to make visible. Attach the disposal records for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Media disposal records for the period, one per retired device, giving the asset identifier, the disposal date, the sanitisation method applied and the destruction certificate or wipe log

title.en: Review the physical access register and withdraw the credentials no longer needed

description.en: Walk the register holder by holder and mark every holder as still required or to be withdrawn, checking each against the access the person's current role needs and paying particular attention to leavers, role changes and contractors whose engagement has ended. Withdraw the credentials marked for removal and record the date each was returned or deactivated, so the review ends in a change rather than a signature. Attach the completed review showing the decision per holder, who confirmed it, and the deactivation dates.

evidenceHint.en: Completed physical access review showing each credential holder marked retained or withdrawn and naming who confirmed each decision, with the deactivation or return date recorded against every withdrawal

text.en: Export the current holder list from the badge system and the key register.
Confirm or reject each holder against the access their current role needs.
Check the list against the leavers and contract endings for the period.
Deactivate or collect each credential marked for withdrawal.
Record the deactivation or return date against every withdrawn credential.

title.en: Review the sub-service organisation's current attestation for physical security exceptions

description.en: For every facility on the list operated by another organisation, obtain the current attestation report and read what it says about physical access control and media handling, rather than filing it unread. Record the period the report covers, whether it is still current at the date of review, and any exception or carve-out that bears on the entity's own data. Attach the attestation together with the note recording what was read and what it left uncovered.

evidenceHint.en: Sub-service organisation attestation covering physical security, filed with a dated note recording the period covered, its currency at review, and any exception affecting in-scope data

templates.title: Network segmentation and boundary protection
templates.description: Separate the production environment from corporate and development networks, restrict inbound and outbound traffic to what is required, deny administrative access from the public internet outside a controlled path, and review the rule set for drift. Implements SOC 2 CC6.1.

title.en: Map the production, corporate and development networks and the enforcement point on each boundary

description.en: Draw the zones this control requires kept apart and, for every boundary between them, name the device or service that enforces it — firewall, security group, peering connection, or the router at a site. Record which zone each in-scope system sits in, including build agents and administrative jump hosts, which are the systems most often left straddling two zones and therefore the ones that quietly join them. Attach the network zone map with the list of enforcement points.

evidenceHint.en: Network zone map naming the production, corporate and development zones, the systems sitting in each, and the enforcement point on every boundary between them

title.en: Record the inbound and outbound traffic permitted across each boundary and why it is required

description.en: For every boundary on the map, write down the flows allowed to cross it: source, destination, port or service, direction, and the reason the flow is required. This written intent is what the rule-set review compares the live configuration against, so a rule set with no documented intent makes that review unfalsifiable — anything found can be explained after the fact. Cover outbound flows as well as inbound, since egress is the direction usually left implicit. Attach the documented boundary flow list.

evidenceHint.en: Documented boundary flow list giving, per boundary, each permitted flow with its source, destination, port, direction and the reason it is required

title.en: Define the controlled path for administrative access and the accounts permitted to use it

description.en: Record how an administrator is expected to reach production — the bastion, VPN or proxy that constitutes the controlled path — and which accounts may use it. State plainly that administrative interfaces are not to be reachable from the public internet outside that path, and record any exception together with the compensating restriction that applies to it, so an exception is visible as an exception rather than as ordinary configuration. Attach the administrative access standard with its issue date.

evidenceHint.en: Administrative access standard naming the controlled path, the accounts permitted to use it, and every exception with the compensating restriction applied to it

title.en: Scan the entity's external address ranges for reachable administrative interfaces

description.en: Run the scan from outside the perimeter against every public address range and hostname the entity owns, and record each port and service found answering, so an administrative interface exposed by a rule change is discovered here rather than by somebody else. Compare the result against the administrative access standard and raise a ticket for anything reachable outside the controlled path. Attach the scan output for the period with the disposition recorded against each finding.

evidenceHint.en: External exposure scan output for the period listing every reachable port and service per public address, with a disposition recorded against each administrative interface found

title.en: Compare the live rule set against the documented flows and remove what is broader than needed

description.en: Export the rules from each enforcement point on the review date and match them line by line to the documented flow list: a rule with no matching entry, a rule wider than the flow it serves, and a rule carrying no traffic are the three outcomes to record. Remove or narrow what the comparison rejects and note the change reference against each, so the review ends with a rule set that matches the map rather than a list of observations. Attach the dated rule-set export alongside the comparison.

evidenceHint.en: Dated live rule-set export from every enforcement point with the comparison against the documented flow list, recording per rule whether it was matched, narrowed or removed and the change reference for each alteration

text.en: Export the live rules from each enforcement point on the review date.
Match every rule to an entry on the documented boundary flow list.
Flag rules wider than the flow they serve or carrying no traffic.
Narrow or remove each rule the comparison rejects.
Record the change reference against every rule altered or removed.

templates.title: Vulnerability management and patching
templates.description: Scan infrastructure, container images, and dependencies for known vulnerabilities on a defined schedule, rate findings by severity, and remediate within published SLAs, with exceptions approved and time-bound. Implements SOC 2 CC7.1.

title.en: List the hosts, container images and dependency manifests each scanner covers

description.en: The control names three scan targets and they are usually covered by three different tools, so record which tool covers which target and what it does not reach — hosts absent from the agent's inventory, images built outside the pipeline, dependency manifests in repositories the scanner has no access to. Coverage written as a list makes the gap visible; coverage inferred from a tool being present hides it. Attach the dated coverage list.

evidenceHint.en: Dated scanner coverage list naming, per scan target class, the tool covering it and the assets that tool does not reach

title.en: Publish the severity rating scale and the remediation SLA each severity carries

description.en: Write down how a finding is rated and how long its severity allows before remediation, so that remediating within published SLAs resolves to a date a specific finding can be measured against. Record where the rating comes from — the scanner's own score, or an adjustment the entity makes for exposure or a compensating control — and who may adjust it, since an unrecorded downgrade is the cheapest way to meet any SLA. Attach the published standard with its version and issue date.

evidenceHint.en: Published vulnerability severity and SLA standard giving the remediation window for each severity and the basis on which a rating may be adjusted

title.en: Record the exception route for a finding that will not be fixed within its SLA

description.en: Set out what an exception must carry before it is accepted — the finding, the reason the SLA cannot be met, the compensating control, the approver, and the date the exception expires — and where accepted exceptions are held. This control allows exceptions only where they are approved and time-bound, so an exception with no expiry date is the failure mode the procedure exists to prevent. Attach the exception procedure together with the register it points at.

evidenceHint.en: Vulnerability exception procedure with the exception register it names, showing the fields every accepted exception must carry including its expiry date

title.en: Run the scheduled scans across hosts, images and dependencies and retain the output

description.en: Run each scan on the documented cadence and keep the raw output rather than a summary: the scan date, the targets reached, the targets that failed to scan, and the findings with their ratings. A scan that failed against part of its target list reads identically to a clean scan once summarised, which is why the failed targets belong in the retained evidence. Attach the scan reports for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Scan reports for the period, one per scan target class, showing the scan date, the assets reached, the assets that failed to scan and the findings with their severities

title.en: Track every finding to closure against the SLA its severity sets

description.en: Keep one register row per finding carrying its severity, the date it was raised, the date its SLA falls due, and the closure — the change or patch reference that fixed it, or the approved time-bound exception standing in place of a fix. Confirm a closure by re-scanning rather than by the change being merged, because a merged fix that did not reach the running host closes the row and not the vulnerability. Attach the findings register for the period showing each closure and the evidence behind it.

evidenceHint.en: Vulnerability findings register for the period giving, per finding, its severity, raised date, SLA due date and either the fix reference confirmed by re-scan or the approved time-bound exception

text.en: Load the period's scan findings into the register with their severities.
Set the SLA due date for each finding from its severity rating.
Record the change or patch reference against each remediated finding.
Re-scan to confirm the finding no longer reports before closing it.
Link every unclosed finding to its approved, time-bound exception.

title.en: Report the findings past their SLA with the reason and the recovery plan for each

description.en: Take the register's overdue rows and produce the report management is given: the finding, its severity, how long it has been open past its due date, why it has not been fixed, and what will close it and by when. Separate the overdue findings that hold an approved exception from those that hold nothing, since only the second group is an escaped SLA and the two are indistinguishable once counted together. Attach the report as presented, with the date it was given and to whom.

evidenceHint.en: Overdue vulnerability report as presented, listing each finding past its SLA with the days overdue, the reason and the recovery plan, and naming the date it was given and its audience

templates.title: Security event logging, monitoring, and alerting
templates.description: Collect security-relevant logs from the in-scope systems into protected storage, retain them for the committed period, and alert on defined conditions — authentication anomalies, privilege changes, configuration drift — to a monitored destination with a named responder. Implements SOC 2 CC7.1.

title.en: List the in-scope systems and the security log sources each is expected to deliver

description.en: Record, per in-scope system, which logs it should be sending — authentication, privilege change, configuration change — and the source name they arrive under in the log store. This expected-source list is what the periodic delivery check is run against; without it a system that silently stopped sending is indistinguishable from a system that has nothing to say, and both look like a quiet dashboard. Attach the dated source list.

evidenceHint.en: Dated log source list naming, per in-scope system, the security log types expected from it and the source name those logs arrive under

title.en: Record each alert condition with its destination and the responder named for it

description.en: Build the alert catalogue: one row per condition this control names — authentication anomalies, privilege changes, configuration drift — with the rule that detects it, the destination the alert is sent to, and the role or rota named as its responder. A condition firing into a destination nobody watches is the shape the catalogue makes visible, and it is the shape a rule-by-rule configuration review never shows. Attach the catalogue covering every condition currently enabled.

evidenceHint.en: Alert catalogue listing each enabled condition with its detection rule, the destination the alert is sent to and the named responder or rota

title.en: Set the log store's retention period and remove alteration rights from the accounts it records

description.en: Configure the store to hold logs for the period the entity has committed to, and take delete and modify rights on that store away from the operational and administrative accounts whose own activity the logs capture — an administrator who can erase the record of their own action leaves the logs unusable as evidence of anything. Record the retention setting and the resulting permission model. Attach the configuration output showing both.

evidenceHint.en: Log store configuration output showing the retention period set and the permission model, evidencing that the accounts recorded by the logs cannot alter or delete them

title.en: Produce the delivery check naming every expected source silent since the last check

description.en: Run the expected-source list against what the store actually received and record the last event received per source, so a source that stopped delivering is named rather than merely missing from a dashboard. Raise a ticket for each silent source and record the cause once found — a decommissioned system, an expired credential, a failed agent. Attach the delivery check for the period with the ticket reference recorded against each gap.

evidenceHint.en: Log delivery check for the period giving the last event received per expected source, with a ticket reference and the cause recorded against every silent source

title.en: Trigger a test condition and record that the alert reached the named responder

description.en: Fire one of the catalogued conditions deliberately and follow it the whole way: the time it was triggered, the time the alert arrived at its destination, and the responder who acknowledged it. Test the path rather than the rule — an alert rule that fires correctly into a channel nobody reads passes every configuration check there is and wakes nobody. Attach the test record for the period naming the condition exercised.

evidenceHint.en: Alert path test record for the period naming the condition triggered, the trigger and alert times, the destination reached and the responder who acknowledged it

title.en: Check the oldest retained event and the store's access list against the retention commitment

description.en: Query the store for the earliest event it still holds and compare it against the retention period committed to, since a retention setting applied after data had already begun ageing out does not prove the commitment has been met. Re-read the access list at the same time and confirm no account recorded by the logs has regained delete or modify rights through a role change. Attach the query output and the access list, both carrying the review date.

evidenceHint.en: Retention and log store access review showing the earliest retained event date against the committed retention period, with the current access list confirming no recorded account can alter the logs

templates.title: Security incident response
templates.description: Maintain an incident response plan defining severity levels, roles, internal escalation, and customer and regulator notification obligations; record every incident with its timeline and root cause; and exercise the plan at least annually. Implements SOC 2 CC7.1.

title.en: Compile the customer and regulator notification obligations an incident can trigger

description.en: List the notification duties the entity carries: for each, the contract or regulation it comes from, the kind of incident that triggers it, whom notice is owed to, and the deadline that source sets. Take the deadlines from the sources themselves rather than from memory of them, and record where each was read so it can be rechecked when a contract is renewed. The plan's escalation only works if the clock it runs against is written down. Attach the obligations register with the date it was compiled.

evidenceHint.en: Notification obligations register naming, per obligation, its contract or regulatory source, the triggering incident type, the party owed notice and the deadline that source sets

text.en: Extract the notification clauses from the in-scope customer contracts.
List the regulatory notification duties that apply to the entity.
Record the triggering incident type for each obligation found.
Record the deadline each source sets and where in the source it was read.
Name the party owed notice and the route by which notice is given.

title.en: Define the incident severity levels and the escalation each level triggers

description.en: Write the severity scale the plan runs on: what distinguishes each level from the one below it, who is notified when an incident is declared at that level, and how quickly it escalates internally. Tie the levels to the notification obligations register so that declaring a severity makes the external duties it may engage visible at the moment of declaration rather than after the incident has closed. Attach the severity and escalation section of the plan as approved.

evidenceHint.en: Approved severity and escalation matrix giving, per severity level, its criteria, the internal escalation it triggers and the notification obligations it may engage

title.en: Name the incident response roles and the current holder and deputy of each

description.en: Record who fills each role the plan defines — incident commander, communications, technical lead, legal — with the current holder, a deputy for when the holder is unreachable, and the contact details each is reachable on outside working hours. This roster is the part of the plan that rots fastest, because it changes with every departure while the plan around it stays accurate. Attach the roster with the date it was last confirmed against the current organisation.

evidenceHint.en: Incident response role roster naming the current holder and deputy of each role with out-of-hours contact details and the date the roster was last confirmed

title.en: Record each incident's timeline, notifications and root cause in one record

description.en: For every incident declared, keep a single record carrying the detection time and how it was detected, the severity assigned and any later reassignment, the actions taken with their times, every notification made against the obligation that required it, and the root cause reached at the end. Close the record when the root cause is written, not when service is restored, since the two happen days apart and only the first completes the control. Attach the incident records for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Incident records for the period, one per incident, giving the detection time, the severity assigned, the action timeline, the notifications made against their obligations and the root cause

title.en: Run a tabletop or simulated incident and record what it changed in the plan

description.en: Exercise the plan at least annually against a scenario the responders have not seen, and record the participants, the scenario, the points at which the response stalled, and the timings achieved against the escalation the plan promises. The output that matters is the change list — the contacts corrected, the steps clarified, the gaps raised as actions with owners and dates. Attach the exercise record together with the plan changes that came out of it.

evidenceHint.en: Incident exercise record naming the scenario, the participants and the timings achieved, with the plan changes and actions arising, each carrying an owner and a date

title.en: Re-approve the response plan after confirming its contacts, escalation and deadlines are current

description.en: Read the plan against the role roster, the notification obligations register and the actions left by the last exercise, and correct what has moved — a departed role holder, a contract whose notification deadline changed, a step the exercise showed does not work. Route the corrected plan through the approval path the plan itself carries, and record the version and the approval date. Attach the approved plan alongside a note of what changed since the previous version.

evidenceHint.en: Approved incident response plan carrying its version and approval date, filed with a change note recording what was corrected since the previous version

templates.title: Backup and restoration testing
templates.description: Back up in-scope data on a schedule that meets the committed recovery point objective, protect backups against modification and deletion, and test restoration at least annually by actually recovering data and verifying its integrity. Implements SOC 2 CC7.1.

title.en: Record every in-scope dataset with the recovery point objective committed for it

description.en: Work through the production systems in scope and list the datasets each holds — application databases, object storage, configuration stores and the log stores an investigation would need. For each row record the system it belongs to, the recovery point objective committed for it, the retention required and where its backup copies are held. This register is the population every later task in this control samples, so a dataset missing here is one no backup job will ever be reconciled against. Attach the register dated at the point it was compiled.

evidenceHint.en: Dated backup register: dataset, owning system, committed recovery point objective, retention period and backup storage location

text.en: List the datasets held by each production system in scope.
Record the recovery point objective committed for each dataset.
Record the retention period and where the backup copies are held.
Name the team accountable for each dataset's backup job.
Date the register and hold it as the population later tasks sample.

title.en: Set each backup job's schedule and retention to meet the recorded recovery point objective

description.en: Take each row of the register and configure the backup job that serves it so the interval between successful backups cannot exceed the committed recovery point objective, and so copies are kept for the recorded retention. Where a job cannot meet the objective, record the shortfall against that register row rather than adjusting the objective to fit the job. Attach the exported job configuration showing schedule, retention and target for every dataset in the register.

evidenceHint.en: Exported backup job configuration per register row, showing the schedule, the retention and the backup target

title.en: Restrict deletion and modification of backup copies to accounts outside routine operations

description.en: Configure the backup repository so the accounts used for day-to-day operations cannot overwrite a backup copy, shorten its retention or delete it — separate credentials, a retention lock or immutability setting, or a separate account boundary, whichever the platform supports. Confirm at the same time that the copies are encrypted at rest. Attach the permission listing for the backup repository together with the immutability or retention-lock setting.

text.en: List the accounts that can reach the backup repository today.
Remove delete and overwrite rights from routine operational accounts.
Turn on the retention lock or immutability the platform offers.
Confirm the backup copies are encrypted at rest and record the setting.
Export the resulting permission listing as the evidence.

title.en: Reconcile backup completions against the register for the period and investigate every failure

description.en: Pull the backup job history for the period and match it row by row against the register, so a dataset whose job silently stopped is visible rather than merely absent from the failure list. For every failed, skipped or missed run record what caused it, whether the committed recovery point objective was breached, and what was done about it. Attach the completion report with the failure investigations appended.

evidenceHint.en: Backup completion report for the period, one line per register row, with an investigation note against every failed, skipped or missed run

text.en: Export the backup job history covering the whole period.
Match each run back to its row in the backup register.
Flag any register row with no successful run in the period.
Record the cause and resolution of every failed or skipped run.
State whether any failure breached the committed recovery point objective.

title.en: Restore a sample of backed-up data into an isolated environment and verify its integrity

description.en: At least annually, take a real backup copy and recover it into an environment isolated from production, then check the restored data is complete and usable rather than merely present — counts against the source, a checksum or application-level consistency check, and an attempt to actually use the restored system. Record the start and finish times so the duration the restore actually took is on the record. Attach the restoration test record with the verification output and any defect raised.

evidenceHint.en: Restoration test record: dataset restored, environment used, start and finish times, integrity checks performed with their output, and defects raised

text.en: Select the datasets to restore and record why they were chosen.
Restore into an environment isolated from production systems.
Compare the restored data against the source for completeness.
Run an application-level check that the restored data is usable.
Record the start and finish times of the restore attempt.
Raise a defect for anything that did not restore as expected.

templates.title: Software change management and approval
templates.description: Require every production change to be tracked, peer reviewed, tested, and approved by someone other than its author before release, with an emergency path that is documented and reviewed after the fact. Implements SOC 2 CC8.1.

title.en: List every repository and deployment path that can change production

description.en: Enumerate the code repositories, infrastructure repositories and pipelines from which a change can reach production, including any manual or console route that still exists. For each, name the branch that releases, the mechanism that deploys it and the team accountable for it. A path missing from this list is a path the review requirement below will never be applied to, which is how an unreviewed change reaches production while every repository looks protected. Attach the list with the date it was compiled.

evidenceHint.en: Dated list of production change paths: repository or pipeline, releasing branch, deploy mechanism and accountable team

text.en: List the code and infrastructure repositories that deploy to production.
Name the releasing branch and deploy mechanism for each one.
Record any manual or console route that can still change production.
Name the team accountable for each path on the list.

title.en: Configure branch protection to require an approving review from someone other than the author

description.en: For each path on the list, turn on the settings that make an unreviewed change impossible rather than merely discouraged: require a pull request into the release branch, require at least one approving review, and prevent an author's own approval from satisfying that requirement. Record any repository where the platform cannot enforce this and what covers the gap instead. Attach the exported protection settings for every repository rather than a screenshot of one.

text.en: Require a pull request before merging to the release branch.
Require at least one approving review on every pull request.
Prevent an author's own approval from satisfying the requirement.
Export the protection settings for each repository on the list.
Record any repository the platform cannot protect and what covers it.

title.en: Write the emergency change path and the retrospective approval it requires

description.en: Set down, in a document somebody can follow during an incident, who may declare a change an emergency, what has to be recorded at the moment it is made, and the after-the-fact review and approval that must follow — naming who gives that approval and the record that shows it was given. Keep it visibly distinct from the standard path so an auditor can tell which route any given change took. Attach the issued procedure with its version and issue date.

title.en: Collect the automated test and security-check results produced for each production release

description.en: For every release in the period, keep the pipeline run that produced it together with the test results and security checks that ran against that exact commit, so that 'it was tested' can be shown rather than asserted. Where a release skipped a check, record which check and why. Attach the per-release evidence set covering the whole period.

evidenceHint.en: Per-release evidence set for the period: release identifier, commit, pipeline run, test results and security-check outcomes, with a note against any skipped check

title.en: Record the period's emergency changes and the retrospective approval given to each

description.en: List the changes that reached production without the standard review, taking the list from the deployment record rather than from what people remember declaring. For each, record who declared the emergency, what changed, why the standard path could not be used, and the retrospective approval that followed with its approver and date. Attach the emergency change log for the period with each approval referenced from its entry.

evidenceHint.en: Emergency change log for the period: change, declarer, justification, date, and the retrospective approval with its approver and date

title.en: Sample the period's production changes and confirm each carries an independent approval

description.en: Draw a sample of production releases from the deployment record and trace each back to its change record: an approving review exists, the approver is not the author, the retained test results cover the released commit, and what deployed matches what was approved. Record the sample size and how it was drawn, and raise a deficiency for every exception instead of resolving it in place. Attach the completed sample worksheet.

evidenceHint.en: Completed change sample worksheet: sample size and how drawn, and per release the change record, approver, author, test results and the result of each check

text.en: Draw the sample from the deployment record, not the repository history.
Trace each release back to its change and approval record.
Confirm the approver is not the author of the change.
Confirm the retained test results cover the released commit.
Raise a deficiency for each exception found in the sample.

templates.title: Infrastructure configuration baselines
templates.description: Define hardened configuration baselines for the systems that make up the production environment, apply infrastructure changes through the same reviewed and approved path as code, and detect and correct drift from the baseline. Implements SOC 2 CC8.1.

title.en: Inventory the system classes that make up the production environment

description.en: Group the production estate into the classes a baseline can actually be written for — compute images, container base images, databases, network devices, managed cloud services — and record which running systems belong to each class and which team owns it. The class is the unit the rest of this control works in, so a system belonging to no class is a system no baseline covers and no drift check will ever look at. Attach the inventory with the count of systems in each class.

evidenceHint.en: Production system-class inventory: class, the running systems in it, the owning team and the count per class

text.en: Group the production estate into classes a baseline can cover.
Assign every running production system to exactly one class.
Name the team that owns each class of system.
Record any system that fits no class as a gap to close.

title.en: Document the hardening baseline for each system class and the source it derives from

description.en: For each class in the inventory, write down the configuration settings a system in that class must hold, and name the published benchmark or internal standard the settings come from — including every place you have deliberately deviated and why. A baseline whose provenance is not recorded can be shown to be documented but not to be hardened. Attach the baseline document, versioned and dated, covering every class in the inventory.

evidenceHint.en: Versioned, dated baseline document with one section per system class, giving the required settings, the source standard behind them and every accepted deviation

text.en: Write the required settings for each class in the inventory.
Name the benchmark or internal standard each setting derives from.
Record every deliberate deviation and the reason it was accepted.
Version and date the document so the baseline in force is identifiable.
Confirm every class in the inventory has a section.

title.en: Route production infrastructure changes through version-controlled definitions that require review

description.en: Move the production estate's configuration into definitions held in version control and make the pipeline that applies them the route by which production changes, so console edits stop being the change path. Require the same approving review on an infrastructure change as on a code change. Record any component that still has to be changed by hand and the compensating check that covers it. Attach the repository protection settings together with one merged infrastructure change traced end to end.

title.en: Run drift detection against each baseline and record what drifted and how it was corrected

description.en: On the documented cadence, compare each running system against the baseline for its class and produce the list of deviations — system, setting, baseline value, observed value and when it was detected. Correct each deviation or record it as an accepted exception naming who accepted it, and carry anything still open into the next run so it cannot quietly disappear. Attach the drift report for the period with the correction recorded against each line.

evidenceHint.en: Drift detection report for the period: system, setting, baseline value, observed value, detection date, and the correction or accepted exception recorded against each line

text.en: Run the drift check across every class in the inventory.
Record each deviation with its baseline and observed value.
Correct the deviation or record an accepted exception and its approver.
Carry unresolved deviations forward into the next run.
Attach the report with a correction recorded against every line.

title.en: Sample the period's production infrastructure changes and confirm none bypassed the reviewed path

description.en: Take the cloud or platform activity log for the period, pick out the changes made to production infrastructure and trace each back to a reviewed, version-controlled definition. Console edits and out-of-band changes are exactly what this sample exists to find, so draw it from the platform's own record rather than from repository history, which by construction only contains changes that went the right way. Raise a deficiency for each change with no reviewed definition behind it, and attach the completed sample worksheet.

evidenceHint.en: Completed infrastructure change sample worksheet: sample drawn from the platform activity log, the reviewed definition traced for each change, and the deficiencies raised

templates.title: Vendor due diligence and ongoing monitoring
templates.description: Assess the security posture of vendors and sub-service organisations before onboarding, proportionate to the data and access they receive, put the required contractual terms in place, and re-assess on a risk-based schedule — reviewing their attestation reports and the complementary user entity controls they assume. Implements SOC 2 CC9.1.

title.en: Register every vendor and sub-service organisation with the data and access it receives

description.en: Build the register the rest of this control works from: one row per vendor and per sub-service organisation, recording what data it receives or processes, what access it holds to production or to customer data, the business owner and the service it supports. Sub-service organisations are the rows most often missed, so take them from the vendors' own attestation reports as well as from procurement records. Attach the register with the date it was compiled.

evidenceHint.en: Dated vendor register: vendor, the sub-service organisations behind it, data received, access held, business owner and the service supported

text.en: List every vendor from procurement and expense records.
Add the sub-service organisations named in vendors' attestation reports.
Record what data each one receives or processes.
Record the access each one holds to production or customer data.
Name the business owner accountable for each vendor relationship.

title.en: Define the vendor risk tiers that set assessment depth and re-assessment interval

description.en: Write down the tiers a vendor can fall into, the data-and-access criteria that place a vendor in each one, what an assessment at that tier must cover, and how often a vendor at that tier is re-assessed. This is what makes 'proportionate' and 'risk-based' decidable by somebody other than the person who wrote it. Assign every vendor already in the register to a tier at the same time. Attach the tier definitions together with the register showing each vendor's tier.

text.en: Write the criteria that place a vendor in each tier.
State what an assessment at each tier must cover.
State the re-assessment interval that each tier carries.
Assign every vendor in the register to a tier.

title.en: Complete the assessments due in the period, including every new vendor's before access is granted

description.en: Work the list of assessments the tiers make due in the period: every vendor being onboarded, and every existing vendor whose tier interval has come round. Run the assessment that vendor's tier requires and record the outcome, the risks accepted and any conditions placed on the engagement. For a new vendor the assessment has to be finished before it receives data or access, not after it is already live — where access came first, record that as an exception rather than backdating the assessment. Attach the completed assessment for each vendor, with the assessment date shown against the date access was granted for the new ones.

evidenceHint.en: Completed assessment per vendor assessed in the period, showing the tier applied, the risks accepted, any conditions set, and — for newly onboarded vendors — the assessment date against the date access was granted

text.en: List the vendors onboarded and those whose tier interval fell due.
Run the assessment the vendor's tier requires.
Record the risks accepted and any conditions placed on the engagement.
Record the assessment date against the date access was granted.

title.en: Verify the security, confidentiality and breach-notification terms are executed before onboarding

description.en: Check that the executed contract for each vendor onboarded in the period carries the security, confidentiality and breach-notification terms the engagement requires, and a data-processing agreement where personal data is involved. Record the clause reference for each term rather than asserting the contract is adequate, so a reviewer can find the term without reading the whole agreement. Attach the extract of executed terms per vendor with its signature date.

evidenceHint.en: Per-vendor extract of the executed contract citing the security, confidentiality and breach-notification clauses, the data-processing agreement where applicable, and the signature date

title.en: Obtain each critical vendor's current attestation report and record the exceptions it discloses

description.en: Collect the current attestation report for every vendor whose tier requires one, check the period the report covers against your own reporting period so a gap between them is visible, and write down the exceptions and qualified opinions it discloses along with what each one means for the service you rely on. Where no report exists, record what was accepted in its place and who accepted it. Attach each report with the dated review note against it.

evidenceHint.en: Each critical vendor's current attestation report with a dated review note giving the period covered, the exceptions disclosed, their impact on the service relied on, and the conclusion reached

text.en: Request the current report from every vendor whose tier requires one.
Check the report period against your own reporting period for gaps.
List the exceptions and qualified opinions the report discloses.
Record what each exception means for the service you rely on.
Record what was accepted where no report could be obtained.

title.en: Map the complementary user entity controls each attestation assumes to an owner here

description.en: Take the complementary user entity controls listed in each vendor's attestation report — the things the report assumes you are doing — and record, for each one, the control on your side that satisfies it and the person who owns that control. Anything with no owner on this side is an assumption the vendor's report is silently relying on, and it is the part of an attestation review most often skipped. Attach the mapping with the unmatched items listed separately.

evidenceHint.en: Complementary user entity control mapping: each control the report assumes, the control operating here that satisfies it, its owner, and a separate list of the items with nothing behind them

text.en: Extract the complementary user entity controls from each report.
Match each one to a control operating on your side.
Name the owner accountable for each matched control.
List every complementary control with nothing behind it.
Raise the unmatched items for treatment as a gap.

templates.title: Business continuity and disaster recovery
templates.description: Maintain business continuity and disaster recovery plans covering the in-scope services, with recovery objectives that match the commitments made to customers, and test them at least annually against a realistic disruption scenario. Implements SOC 2 CC9.1 and CC7.1.

title.en: Scope the services the continuity and recovery plans must cover, with their dependencies

description.en: List the in-scope services and, for each one, the infrastructure, data stores and third parties it cannot run without — so a plan that recovers a service into a dependency which is itself still down is visible before the exercise rather than during it. Record the recovery commitment made to customers for each service alongside it. Attach the scope list with its dependency column completed for every service.

evidenceHint.en: Service scope list: in-scope service, its infrastructure, data and third-party dependencies, and the recovery commitment made to customers

text.en: List the services in scope for continuity and recovery.
Record the infrastructure and data each service cannot run without.
Record the third parties each service depends on to operate.
Record the recovery commitment made to customers for each service.

title.en: Reconcile each service's documented RTO and RPO against the commitment made to customers

description.en: Put the recovery time and recovery point objectives written in the plan side by side with what the customer contracts, service descriptions and public commitments actually say, service by service. Where the two differ, record the difference and how it is resolved — the objective is tightened, or the commitment is corrected — rather than leaving two numbers in circulation for an auditor to find. Attach the reconciliation showing both values and the resolution for every service.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation table: service, documented RTO and RPO, committed RTO and RPO, the difference and how each difference was resolved

title.en: Publish the recovery procedure for each in-scope service, naming the roles that execute it

description.en: Write the steps that recover each service on the scope list — the order dependencies come back, who decides to invoke the plan, who executes each step and how they are reached — and issue it somewhere the people who need it can still open when their usual systems are down. Version and date the procedure so the copy in force during an exercise is identifiable afterwards. Attach the issued plan with its version and its distribution record.

text.en: Write the recovery steps for each service on the scope list.
Set the order in which dependencies must be recovered.
Name who declares an invocation and who executes each step.
Record how each named role is contacted when systems are down.
Issue the plan somewhere reachable during an outage and record distribution.

title.en: Exercise the plan against a realistic disruption scenario and record what was recovered

description.en: At least annually, run the plan against a scenario resembling a disruption the service could actually suffer, with the people who would really execute it rather than a reading of the document. Record what was recovered, in what order, how long each step took against its objective, and what did not work — an exercise that produces no findings usually means the scenario was too kind. Attach the exercise record with the timings and the findings list.

evidenceHint.en: Exercise record: scenario used, date, participants, services recovered, elapsed time per service against its objective, and the findings raised

text.en: Choose a scenario resembling a disruption the service could suffer.
Run the exercise with the people who would really execute the plan.
Record the order in which services and dependencies came back.
Time each recovery step against the objective set for it.
Record every step that did not work as the plan describes.
List the findings the exercise produced before closing it out.

title.en: Revise the plan from the exercise findings and raise each shortfall in the deficiency register

description.en: Take each finding from the exercise and either correct the plan, fix the underlying capability, or record why neither is being done, then reissue the plan with its version incremented. Every finding that the reissue does not close goes into the deficiency register and the risk register with an owner and a target date, so it stays visible once the exercise report has been filed and forgotten. Attach the reissued plan together with the register entries created from the findings.

evidenceHint.en: Reissued plan with an incremented version, and the deficiency and risk register entries created from the exercise findings, each with an owner and a target date

pack.name: SOC 2 Baseline Pack
pack.description: The common-criteria controls a SOC 2 Type II readiness programme starts from. Reuses the existing pack key deliberately: production already ships SOC2_BASELINE, and a second pack would leave a customer choosing between two SOC 2 offerings. applyCatalogFile only ADDS pack links, so until the seven placeholder SOC2- templates are retired this pack transitionally carries both sets; deleting those templates removes their links by cascade (PackTemplateLink.template onDelete: Cascade).
